This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 17-02-2022 at about 7.30 a.m., the Petitioner was proceeding towards his village Banahalli from Srinivasapura by riding his motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-40-ED-6980 and when he reached near Doddagurki cross on Srinivasapura - Mulabagal road, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, the driver of the Ashok Leyland Dost Light goods vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-07-A-8544 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle) came from opposite direction with high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Petitioner's motorcycle.

entities.text: Ashok Leyland Dost Light goods vehicle
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the accident Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He was immediately taken to Government Hospital, Mulabagal, wherein he has taken first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an outpatient and on the same day he was shifted to R.L.Jalappa hospital, Kolar, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that Petitioner has spent Rs.50,000/- for treatment, medicines,
conveyance and other charges.
At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 35 years, working as a coolie and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries he has lost his earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- insured and Respondent No.2-Insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed the written statement.
The Respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.

4. The Respondent No.2 has filed its written statement and contended that the petitioner was not having DL and the driver of the offending goods vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the driver has violated the policy terms and conditions.

Respondent no2 further has disputed that the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner,
avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by him, expenses incurred by him and disability suffered by him and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was riding his Honda Dio Scooter bearing No. KA-40-ED- 6980 on 17-02-2022, about 7.30 a.m., near Doddagurki cross, on Srinivavsapura- Mulabagal road,

2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order ?

6. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case, 2 witnesses are examined as PW-2 and 3 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.17 respectively.

7. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
8.

My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9.
ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 17-02-2022 at about 7.30 a.m., he was proceeding towards his village Banahalli from Srinivasapura by riding his motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA-40-ED-6980 and when he reached near Doddagurki cross on Srinivasapura - Mulabagal road, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, the driver of the Ashok Leyland Dost Light goods vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-07-A-8544 came from opposite direction with high speed and in rash and negligent manner, lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the motorcycle and caused the accident.

sentences.text: Thereby the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous head and other injuries.

The petitioner has taken first aid treatment at Govt.hospital, Mulabagal, thereafter he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he was treated as an in patient and on the same day he was came to R.L,Jalappa hospital, Kolar.
As per X-ray petitioner has sustained major head injuries.
10. In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.1 to 10.
To support of his claim, Junior Executive Officer at Medical Records department at R.L.Jalappa hospital was examined as Pw-2 and he has produced the 4 documents at Ex.P.11 to 14.

Further, Dr.Veeresha U Mathad was examined as PW-3 and he has produced the 3 documents at Ex.P.15 to 17.
11.
On perusal of police and medical records, it appears that the petitioner sustained injuries in a RTA.
The police records show that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle the accident was caused.
As a result, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
There is no materials to disbelieve or rebut the evidence of the petitioner and charge sheet has been filed against the offending vehicle.
Therefore, this tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Ashok Leyland Dost Light goods vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-07-A-8544.

12. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P.5 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained the following injuries:
1. Sutured laceration over right occipital region of 14 x 3 cms.
2. Abrasion of 3 x 3 cm.
Over right side of forehead.

Over Left side of forehead.
4. Peri-orbital edema and swelling over right eye.
5. Upper eyelid swelling over left eye.
The doctor opined that the above injuries are grievous in nature.
13. Due to the accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was taken to NIMHANS, Bengaluru.
Wherein, he was treated as an outpatient and on the same date he was admitted in R.L. Jalappa hospital from 17.2.22 to 23.2.22.

He has stated that at the time of accident,
he was a coolie and earning a sum of .25,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of income.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.

14. The Petitioner has examined Medical record technician at R L Jalappa hospital, Bengaluru as PW-2 and he has produced MLC register extract, police intimation memo and case sheet at Ex.P.12 to 14.
15.

PW-3 Dr.Veeresha U Mathad. B. neuro surgeon at Manipal hospital, Bengaluru, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA and treated at Baptist hospital, Bengaluru and Petitioner has sustained RIGHT PARIETAL SUBARAVHOID, HAEMORRAGE, RIGHT OCCIPTAL BONE FRACTURE WITH UNDERLING SPECT OF CONTUSION, MULTIPLE SMALL INTRACRANIAL AIRFOCI IN POSTERIOR CRANIAL FOSSA and he was admitted at RL Jalappa hospital and research center for treatment of moderate traumatic brain injury. PW-3
has examined the Petitioner clinically and taken MRI scan while assessing disability.
He found that Petitioner complains of headache, right ear pain,memory loss, forgets things, forgets names conversations and difficult to identify and recognize people.
Get angry easily, giddiness, gets irritated with loud noise or sounds and do his routine work as earlier.
On examination he has assessed the total permanent physical impairment due to head injury at 40%.
16. PW-3 in his cross-examination has stated that he has not treated the Petitioner.
He denied that the disability may have chances to reduce in future.
He also denied the suggestion that the petitioner can do his work without any assistant.
It is pertinent to note that PW3 has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.

Therefore, considering that the grievous injuries is on the head and considering the difficulties and evidence of PW-3 and also by considering the age of the Gangappa.G vs Basavaraj S.S on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103387239/

17. In the petition the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 35 years and in the wound certificate and other medical record it was mentioned age of the petitioner as 35 years.
Wherein

Ex .P.9 Aadhar card shows that he was born on 1/1/86, the same is considered as age of the deceased as on the date of accident as 36 years and the multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 15.
18.
The age of the petitioner is 36 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in R.L.Jalappa hospital at Kolar.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was doing coolie work and was earning Rs.25,000/-P.M.
Due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to do his work and is unable to do his work as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
However, the petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his income.
In the absence of material with regard to source of income, the tribunal has to be considered the national income chart of the Lok Adalath.
19. On perusal of the record, it appears that the age of the petitioner as on date of the alleged accident was about 36 years.
The alleged accident has taken place in the year 2022, the notional income of the injured could be assessed at Rs 15,500/- Per Month.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
20. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Looking into the nature of injuries, it definitely affects the working capacity of any person.
As the Petitioner is a coolie, considering nature of injury and doctor's evidence the total functional disability of the Petitioner is considered at 9%.
21. In case of Pappu Deo Yadav v Naresh Kumar and others 2020 SCC online SC 752 the Apex court held that in the case of permanent partial disability amount towards future prospects can be awarded .

entities.text: Pappu Deo Yadav v Naresh Kumar and others 2020 SCC online SC 752
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said preposition of law has been reiterated by the Hon'ble High court reported in 2020 SCC online KAR 1446 between Alameli Bai V/s Managing Director KSRTC, wherein the Hon'ble High court of Karnataka has held that in case of functional disability cases, future prospects can be awarded.

entities.text: Alameli Bai V/s Managing Director KSRTC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus the petitioner is entitled for the amount towards future prospects.
22. Keeping in view above said dictum this tribunal concludes that the petitioner was 36 years as on the date of the alleged accident.
As such, 40% of the future prospects is to be added to the annual income.
Thus effective notional income comes to 15,500 + 40% ( Rs. 6,200) = 21,700.
Thus effective income comes to Rs. 21,700/- per month.

23. Further the petitioner was aged about 36 years as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 15.
the national income taken as Rs 21,700 x 12 x 15 x 9/100= Rs 3,51,540/- towards loss of future income.

24. Pain and sufferings: So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the fact that the Petitioner has sustained head injuries and was inpatient for a period of Gangappa.G vs Basavaraj S.S on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103387239/
5 7 days which caused him to immeasurable mental agony and pain, I am of the opinion that an amount of .20,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head pain and sufferings.
25. Loss of amenities of life:
For loss of amenities of life undoubtedly Petitioner is sure to suffer in his day today activities and face hardships.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded .20,000/- under loss of amenities of life.
26. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.14 amounting to 56,090/-.
The Respondent has not seriously disputed the medical bills.
Hence, Petitioner is awarded compensation of 56,090/- towards Medical Expenses.
27. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.8-Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was treated as an inpatient at R L Jalappa hospital, Kolar from 17-02-2022 to 23-02- 2022 i.e, for a period of 7 days.

Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .10,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
28. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to loss of earnings during treatment,
considering 7 days admission in the hospital as inpatient and around 1 month for rest is considered and loss of earnings during treatment is calculated for 1 month.

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .15,500/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .15,500 x 1 = 15,500/-.
29.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

3. Loss of amenities . 20,000/-
